newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SmarTone seen making little headway from IPO price.
newsitem.headline: SmarTone seen making little headway from IPO price.

text.p: SmarTone Telecommunications Holdings Ltd shares are expected to notch up only limited gains after their listing in Hong Kong on Thursday, since their issue price is already considered expensive, analysts said.
The mobile telephone operator offered 84 million shares globally of which 15 percent was offered in Hong Kong and 85 percent in an international placement.
Market sources said on Monday the shares were priced at HK$17.25 (US$2.23) a share, at the low end of a HK$17.25 to HK$21.25 per share range. Dealing in the shares is due to begin on Thursday.
"We see limited upside (for the shares) because the issue price was a bit high for local investors," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities H.K. Ltd.
The subscription period for the shares closed last Friday and market sources said the subscription rate was fairly low for both the international and local portions.
The Hong Kong flotation was several times oversubscribed and the international placement was also oversubscribed, they said.
"The subscription rate was on the lower end of expectations," said Sunny Chan, senior research director at Seapower Research.
"The low subscription rate will affect overall sentiment on the stock," he said, adding however that longer term investors should provide good support for the stock near the issue price.
"We don't expect the shares to fall below the issue price but a sharp rally is also unlikely," said Lennon Chan, executive director at Tai Fook Securities.
He said fixing the price at the lower end of the price range would help stabilise the share price movement, despite the low subscription rate.
Analysts said competition in the Personal Communications Services (PCS) market could hurt the company's future earnings.
"Long term fundamentals are not very encouraging," said Marvin Lo, utilities analyst at Amsteel Research.
He pointed to cellular operator SmarTone's failure in September to secure a PCS license during the award of six 10-year PCS licenses by the Hong Kong government.

But analysts said SmarTone's potential for penetrating the mainland telecommunications industry and expectations of strong support from its main shareholders, underpinned the interest shown by overseas investors.

SmarTone is 40 percent owned by Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd, 30 percent by AT&T Wireless Communications, 15 percent by ABC Communications (Holdings) Ltd, and 15 percent by Town Khan Ltd, a unit of China's Ministry of Post and Telecommunications.
